title: Beautiful Pairs
summary: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays of the same length, find a pair of indices (i, j) where i < j, such that the sum of the absolute differences between the elements at these indices in both arrays is the smallest.
statement: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays of the same length, find a pair of indices (i, j) where i < j, such that the sum of the absolute differences between the elements at these indices in both arrays is the smallest. If there are multiple pairs with the same smallest sum, return the pair with the smaller lexicographical order.
constraints: Break equal-distance ties by the lexicographically smallest [i,j].
hints: Sort points by x and recursively solve the left and right halves.
Only points within the current best x-distance of the split can improve the answer.
Sort that strip by y and compare forward until the y gap exceeds the best distance.
Every closest pair is either contained in a half or crosses the split and therefore appears in the strip scan; tuple comparison enforces index ties.
